title: Fire Protection — Cargo Smoke Warning and Extinguishing Discharge

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Flight crew procedure for a cargo compartment smoke warning, covering the discharge of the extinguishing agent, the suppression time available and the diversion decision that follows.

sections.purpose: This entry gives the flight crew procedure for a cargo compartment smoke warning, the discharge of the extinguishing agent and the planning that must follow the discharge.
sections.description: A cargo smoke warning is treated as a fire until it is proven otherwise, and the extinguishing agent is discharged into the affected compartment on the ECAM action. The agent suppresses rather than extinguishes: it holds the compartment below the condition needed for combustion for a defined period, and that period is what determines how far the aircraft can go before it must be on the ground. The available suppression time is published for the aircraft configuration and depends on the compartment, the agent quantity and the compartment leakage. It is not extended by any crew action. On the longer fuselage variant the published time was extended after test evidence showed the compartment leakage to be lower than originally assumed; crews on a mixed fleet must use the figure for the aircraft they are flying and not the one they remember.
sections.crew_procedure: Complete the ECAM actions and confirm the discharge. Establish the suppression time available for the aircraft configuration and note the time of discharge. Plan an immediate diversion to an aerodrome that can be reached, and be on the ground, within the available suppression time; do not plan to the limit of it. Do not open the affected compartment on the ground until the fire service has taken control. Report the warning, the discharge and the elapsed time before landing.

type_data.crew_action: Complete the ECAM actions, note the discharge time and plan a diversion inside the available suppression time.
